# Protocols

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **Spend every single-use item (authorization code, device code, auth_req_id, request_uri, initial access token, paused-flow state, rotating refresh token) atomically through its row's concurrency token, answer the loser of a race as a second spend with the protocol error for a used item (such as invalid_grant 400), and never retry a spend after losing the race.** A concurrent second spend must get the same answer as a sequential one. A spend depends on what it read, so retrying after a lost race would spend the item twice. Letting the exception escape gives a 500. *Check:* In consume-once, revoke-once or replace-once code, check that the store-neutral concurrency exception around update and save is caught and mapped to the 'not found or already used' result, that no caller lets it escape as a 500, and that the save isn't wrapped in a concurrency retry. <sub>Identity ADR-1012; Identity ADR-1222</sub>
- **Revoke grants only through the shared grant service, as an idempotent soft revoke that stamps a revoked time and keeps the row, and retry by reading again when the save loses a concurrency race. Have the runtime treat a revoked grant as inactive.** A revocation is correct whatever state its caller read, so a lost race must be retried, not failed (500 where RFC 7009 wants 200) or reported as success with the grant still active. A soft revoke leaves an audit trail and makes DELETE safe to repeat. *Check:* Flag hard deletes of grant rows, revocation times stamped directly through a store, a concurrency exception caught and turned into success, no retry on a lost race, a non-204 answer for an already-revoked grant, or an active-grant lookup that ignores the revoked time. <sub>Identity ADR-1020; Identity ADR-1222</sub>
- **Compare `redirect_uri` exactly: keep it as the original string in messages, requests and stored state (parse a `Uri` only briefly to inspect a part), refuse a request with more than one `redirect_uri` value, and at the token endpoint compare it ordinally with the authorization request's value, treating an empty value as missing. Never relax matching to a prefix or normalized form.** RFC 6749 §4.1.3 requires identical values, and a parsed `Uri` or a joined multi-value no longer equals what the client sent, so host case, trailing slashes or user info would slip through. *Check:* Look for `Uri`-typed redirect URI members, serialization through `AbsoluteUri`/`ToString()`, `StringValues` joined or first-taken without rejecting duplicates, case-insensitive, `Uri` or prefix comparisons, and empty strings treated as present. <sub>Identity ADR-1203; Identity ADR-1148</sub>
- **Redirect after logout only to a `post_logout_redirect_uri` that ordinally and exactly matches one of the client's registered `post_logout_redirect_uris` and passes the redirect-URI kind check; otherwise render a confirmation page.** Exact matching prevents open redirects from the end-session endpoint. *Check:* Look for case-insensitive, prefix or normalized comparisons in logout redirect code, or a redirect when no registered URI matches. <sub>Identity ADR-1380</sub>
- **Make the end-session endpoint ask the end user to confirm whenever an OP login is present and the request has no valid `id_token_hint` whose `sid` ordinally equals the login's `sid`.** RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 §2 requires the prompt, which closes logout CSRF from cross-site links and forms. *Check:* Flag end-session paths that end the session without a matching-`sid` hint and without confirmation, or non-ordinal `sid` comparisons. <sub>Identity ADR-1380</sub>
- **On the server, treat a `code_challenge` without a `code_challenge_method` as having no method rather than defaulting it, refuse methods the operator hasn't listed (authorization endpoint) or that have no registered transformation (token endpoint), return `invalid_request` for a missing or malformed challenge at the authorization and PAR endpoints, and return `invalid_grant` for a missing, malformed or mismatched verifier or a verifier presented with a code that has no challenge.** OAuth 2.1 makes the method required, defaulting would revive RFC 7636's `plain` default, and accepting a verifier for an unbound code lets a PKCE downgrade through (RFC 9700 §4.8.2). *Check:* Look for a missing method defaulted to `plain` or `S256`, any registered method accepted without the configured list, the wrong error code on a PKCE failure, or a token handler that ignores a verifier when the code wasn't bound. <sub>Identity ADR-1144</sub>
- **In an OAuth client, send every authorization-code request with PKCE `S256` and a freshly generated random `state` and `nonce`, and require the token request to carry `code_verifier`. Fail with a provider exception when the provider's `code_challenge_methods_supported` is present and lacks `S256`; accept the provider when the list is absent.** PKCE binds the code to the initiator and fresh state and nonce defend against CSRF and replay. A missing list doesn't mean S256 is unsupported. *Check:* Look for an optional `code_verifier`, a missing or `plain` challenge, reused or non-random state or nonce, rejection of a provider without the list, or a list without S256 being ignored. <sub>Identity ADR-1285; Identity ADR-1275; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **In an OAuth client callback, compare the RFC 9207 `iss` response parameter with the issuer pinned in the stored login transaction before exchanging the authorization code, and require it whenever the provider advertises `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported`.** Checking `iss` first stops a mix-up attack from sending the code to the wrong provider's token endpoint. *Check:* Flag callbacks that call the token endpoint before the `iss` comparison, never check it, or take the expected issuer from the response instead of the stored transaction. <sub>Identity ADR-1290; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **When validating an ID token, require `iss` to equal the discovered issuer, `aud` to contain the client id, `exp` and `iat` to be present, `azp` (when present) to equal the client id, `typ` (when present) to be `JWT`, and `nonce` and any expected `sub` to match ordinally, each mismatch with its own failure code.** OpenID Connect Core requires these checks before a client trusts the identity, and the caller needs to know which one failed. *Check:* Look for ID-token validation that skips any check, treats `exp` or `iat` as optional, ignores a present `azp` or `typ`, compares nonce or sub case-insensitively, or reports mismatches under a generic code. <sub>Identity ADR-1273; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **When the client requested `max_age`, require the ID token's `auth_time` to be a NumericDate and reject the token once now exceeds `auth_time + max_age` plus the allowed clock skew.** OIDC Core requires the client to enforce the `max_age` it requested. *Check:* Look for `max_age` handling that accepts a missing or non-numeric `auth_time` or omits the elapsed-time check. <sub>Identity ADR-1273; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **In code-flow ID-token validation, accept a missing `at_hash`, `c_hash` or `s_hash`, but when the claim is present and the caller has the matching value, require it to verify. Compute these hashes with the signing algorithm's defined token-hash function, never from the `alg` name's suffix or a bare `HashAlgorithmName`.** The claims are optional in the code flow (OIDC Core §3.1.3.6, §3.1.3.8). Ed25519/Ed448 (SHAKE256 with 114 bytes) and polymorphic EdDSA don't hash as their name suggests. *Check:* Flag validation that fails on an absent hash claim or skips a present one, and token-hash code that parses `256`/`384`/`512` from `alg`, switches on alg strings or maps `HashAlgorithmName` directly. <sub>Identity ADR-1273; Identity ADR-1392</sub>
- **Validate a back-channel logout token per Back-Channel Logout 1.0 §2.6: `typ` when present is `logout+jwt`; at least one of `sub`/`sid` is present and each present one is non-empty; `sid` is present when `backchannel_logout_session_required` applies; `events` is an object whose `http://schemas.openid.net/event/backchannel-logout` member is an object; `nonce` is absent; `jti` is a non-empty string; and signature, `iss`, `aud` and `iat` pass as for other provider JWTs.** A logout token has different required claims and `typ` from an ID token, and these checks stop an ID token being presented as a logout token. *Check:* Look for missing `typ`, `events`, nonce-absence or sub/sid checks, or empty `sub`/`sid` accepted. <sub>Identity ADR-1274; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **For any token or delivery refused on replay (logout-token `jti`, webhook or event dedupe keys), validation only looks the key up; record it only after every other check passed and the caller has acted on it. A back-channel logout endpoint validates, ends the sessions, records the `jti`, then answers 200 with `Cache-Control: no-store`; when the request or token is invalid, keys can't be read or a session can't be ended, it answers 400 without recording.** The sender retries a failed delivery with the same token, so recording early turns the retry into a refused replay and the sessions are never ended (Back-Channel Logout 1.0 §2.8). *Check:* Flag a replay-store add inside a validate method, recording before the work completes or on an error path, a 200 when ending sessions failed, a missing no-store, or any check moved after the replay write. <sub>Identity ADR-1274; Identity ADR-1280; Identity ADR-1293; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **In a back-channel logout receiver, find sessions through `sid`/`sub` indexes rather than scanning the store, and end only sessions that match the token's issuer, its `sid` when present, and the receiving client. Require `sid` by default and accept `sub`-only tokens only when an explicit option turns that off.** Scanning doesn't scale, the matching checks stop one token ending another issuer's or client's sessions, and a `sub`-only default lets one provider session end every session of the user. *Check:* Look for store enumeration, sessions ended without issuer, sid or client filtering, or a session-required option defaulting to false. <sub>Identity ADR-1293; Identity ADR-1442</sub>
- **Run token validation in a fixed order: algorithm policy, decrypt, signature, issuer, audience, lifetime, then the encryption requirement, a replicated header `iss` and `typ`, then claim checks. When a JWE header replicates `iss` (RFC 7519 §5.3), require it to be a string equal to the expected issuer or fail with `invalid_issuer`.** No check may run before the algorithm policy, and a mismatched replicated header must not be ignored. *Check:* Look for checks reordered ahead of algorithm policy, or JWE handling that ignores a header `iss` or accepts a non-string or mismatched one. <sub>Identity ADR-1280</sub>
- **Set an access token's `aud` to the identifiers of the enabled resource servers owning its effective scopes, falling back to the client id only for a scopeless token so no token lacks an audience; always set an ID token's `aud` to the client id.** An audience equal to the client id confuses requester and recipient so a resource server can't tell tokens meant for it; OpenID Connect fixes the ID-token audience. *Check:* Flag access-token minting that sets `aud` to the client id while scopes exist or can emit no `aud`, and ID-token creation deriving `aud` from resources or scopes. <sub>Identity ADR-1026</sub>
- **Treat RFC 8707 `resource` values only as a narrowing of the scope-derived audience: match them ordinally against known resource identifiers, never grant access to a resource the client has no scope for, reject unknown, unauthorized or non-matching values with `invalid_target`, and at code redemption refuse a `resource` the authorization request didn't authorize. Don't add discovery metadata advertising resource indicators.** Narrowing gives least privilege and FAPI's audience binding; a token request may never widen the authorization. Neither RFC 8707 nor RFC 8414 defines such metadata. *Check:* Look for audiences or scopes added because of `resource`, invalid values ignored, an error other than `invalid_target`, case-insensitive or URI-syntax matching, a missing subset check at redemption, or new resource-indicator discovery fields. <sub>Identity ADR-1026</sub>
- **Resolve audience, `resource` narrowing and other token-minting policy at one shared token-minting path that every grant type uses.** A single choke point gives every grant the same enforcement. *Check:* Flag a new grant or token path that mints an access token outside the shared token service or duplicates its audience logic. <sub>Identity ADR-1026</sub>
- **Emit `aud` as a string for one audience and an array for several, and validate it by membership: when the verifier names no audiences, refuse a token that carries `aud`; when it names some, require `aud` to contain one; a token without `aud` is valid only for a verifier that names none.** RFC 7519 §4.1.3 and RFC 8392 allow an array, and some tokens (such as status lists) legitimately have no `aud`. *Check:* Flag string-equality audience checks that reject arrays, checks skipped when the configured list is empty, emission always in one form, or `aud` always required. <sub>Identity ADR-1026; Identity ADR-1410</sub>
- **Validate a request object's `aud` against the configured expected audience or, when none is configured, the authorization server's issuer, and refuse one without `aud` with `invalid_request_object`. Don't report a missing `typ` `oauth-authz-req+jwt` requirement when `iss` is checked against the client, `aud` against the issuer, and the signature is verified.** An unchecked `aud` lets a request object meant for another server be replayed; requiring the explicit `typ` would refuse every OIDC Core client and the conformance suite. *Check:* Look for JAR loading that skips `aud` when nothing is configured or accepts a missing `aud`; before raising a `typ` finding confirm the iss/aud/signature checks. <sub>Identity ADR-1187</sub>
- **Refuse a request object lacking `response_type`, `scope`, `redirect_uri` or `client_id` with `invalid_request_object`, and refuse it when an outer `response_type`, `redirect_uri` or `client_id` was sent and differs; ignore an outer `scope`.** A code must never be sent to one URI and redeemable only with another; OIDC Core §6.1 lets the object's scope supersede the outer one. *Check:* Check required members are enforced, outer values compared for equality when sent, and an outer client_id used only when the object omits it. <sub>Identity ADR-1202</sub>
- **Derive an authorization response's redirect target, response mode and state once per request as a single value, and show an error raised before a safe redirect target is known to the user agent instead of redirecting it.** Later responses, including signed errors, need the verified values, and redirecting before verification sends an error to an unverified URI. *Check:* Look for redirect_uri, response_mode or state recomputed in several places, or errors redirected before the request object or redirect URI is verified. <sub>Identity ADR-1202</sub>
- **In the authorization endpoint's catch-all, translate an exception into a protocol error and deliver it to the client's redirect URI with `state` (RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1) instead of letting it escape as a generic server error.** A client of the authorization endpoint must receive the error at its redirect URI with `state`. *Check:* Check that generic exception handling runs the exception translators and redirects with `error` and `state` once a safe target is known. <sub>Identity ADR-1428</sub>
- **When writing an authorization response to the redirect URI, keep the registered query and add response parameters to it (a response parameter replacing a same-named pair), never carrying request-supplied parameters; in the `Location` header percent-encode only what a header can't carry (non-ASCII, controls, space) and keep any fragment.** RFC 6749 §3.1.2 keeps the registered query, request-supplied parameters must not reach the client inside a response, and the client must receive the response at its URI exactly as sent. *Check:* Flag writers that drop the query, duplicate same-named parameters, append request parameters, build Location from `Uri.AbsoluteUri` or fully re-encode, or strip the fragment. <sub>Identity ADR-1203</sub>
- **Return an authorization response redirect with HTTP 303 and a login challenge redirect with 302, never 307.** A 307 replays a POST body, including credentials, to the next location; FAPI 2.0 requires 303 and it's correct for every client. *Check:* Flag 307 or a non-303 authorization response redirect. <sub>Identity ADR-1148</sub>
- **Apply protocol rules that are correct for every client unconditionally rather than behind a security profile: single-use codes, exact redirect_uri matching, client assertions and request objects validated with the effective clock skew, and the RFC 9207 `iss` response parameter on by default.** These FAPI 2.0 rules are simply correct; only rules a mandated profile must impose belong in a profile. *Check:* Flag changes that wrap these behaviors in a profile check, allow code reuse, ignore clock-skew settings, or default `iss` off. <sub>Identity ADR-1148</sub>
- **Never gate protocol enforcement on a security-profile name check (such as `profile == "fapi2"`) or a closed set of per-profile flags; express the rule as a registered, typed profile requirement evaluated through the profile catalog.** Consumers and sibling packages add profiles by registering them, so enforcement points must stay profile-agnostic. *Check:* Look for string comparisons, enums, boolean flags or switches on profile identity in endpoint, validation or issuance code. <sub>Identity ADR-1148</sub>
- **At the authorization endpoint, never authenticate the client: resolve it by `client_id`, read its registered type, and refuse a request carrying `client_secret` with `invalid_request`.** It is a front-channel endpoint, and RFC 6749 §2.3.1 confines `client_secret` to back-channel request bodies. *Check:* Flag credential verification in authorization-endpoint code, or a `client_secret` accepted or silently ignored there. <sub>Identity ADR-1145</sub>
- **Implement each client authentication method as its own handler and descriptor; a handler claims a request only when the client's registered `token_endpoint_auth_method` equals its method, defers (Undefined) otherwise, and once it claims the request a missing or mismatched credential is a conclusive `invalid_client`.** Methods are advertised and registered individually, and a certificate presented only for token binding must not be taken as an authentication attempt; once owned, there is no fallback. *Check:* Flag a descriptor covering several methods, a handler branching to serve several, triggering on the mere presence of a certificate or credential, or falling through after claiming. <sub>Identity ADR-1102; Identity ADR-1173</sub>
- **A JWT client-assertion handler reads `client_assertion` and `client_assertion_type` only from a form POST body, defers unless the type is exactly `urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer`, requires `iss` and `sub` both present and equal, locates the client by `sub`, and doesn't require a separate `client_id` parameter.** Client authentication is a strategy collection, OIDC Core §9 pins iss == sub == client_id, and FAPI private_key_jwt clients send only the assertion. *Check:* Look for assertions read from query or headers, a missing type check, a missing iss/sub equality, lookup by `iss` alone, or rejection for lack of a `client_id` form parameter. <sub>Identity ADR-1102</sub>
- **When checking a client assertion's `aud` or a DPoP proof's `htu`, compare with the endpoint URL the tenant publishes, built the same way discovery builds it, whose authority is the issuer base address or the RFC 8705 mTLS alias; never build it from the request's scheme and Host. By default accept an assertion `aud` of the issuer or that endpoint URL, restricting to the issuer only when a profile such as FAPI requires it.** A URL from the request Host would accept assertions or proofs minted for another server, and OIDC Core §9 allows the endpoint URL as audience. *Check:* Flag comparisons against Host-derived URLs or URLs built differently from discovery, default validation rejecting the endpoint URL, or accepting audiences outside the tenant's published URLs. <sub>Identity ADR-1365</sub>
- **Compare a DPoP proof's `htu` with exactly one published URL: the one under the mTLS alias when the request arrived on the alias's host and port, otherwise the one under the base address; never accept a match against any of a set.** RFC 9449 §4.3 binds a proof to the URL the request was sent to; the Host header only selects among the tenant's own origins. *Check:* Look for `htu` checked against a candidate set, or a Host that can add an origin the tenant doesn't publish. <sub>Identity ADR-1365</sub>
- **When validating a DPoP proof, compare `htm` exactly to the method, compare `htu` with the request URI after removing query and fragment from both and requiring absolute `http`/`https` URIs, check `ath` when an access token is presented, require `jti`, and require `iat` within ±lifetime of now. Answer a required but missing or invalid nonce with `use_dpop_nonce` and a `DPoP-Nonce` header, and invalid proofs with `invalid_dpop_proof`.** These claims bind the proof to one request, moment and token (RFC 9449 §4, §8); on Unix a rooted path like `/token` parses as a `file:` URI. *Check:* Flag `htu` comparisons keeping query or fragment, relative paths parsed with `Uri`, missing `ath`, `jti` or `iat` window checks, or nonce/proof failures with other error codes or no header. <sub>Identity ADR-1176; Identity ADR-1097</sub>
- **Create a fresh DPoP proof per request with header `typ: dpop+jwt`, `alg` and the public `jwk` only (no `kid`, no private members), `htu` without query or fragment and set to the endpoint actually called (including an mTLS alias), a random 128-bit `jti`, `iat` from `TimeProvider`, signed through the asynchronous path. Token-endpoint proofs use `htm` POST and no `ath`; resource proofs include `ath` and the cached nonce.** RFC 9449 proofs embed the public key, `ath` exists only for proofs that present an access token, and each proof must be new. *Check:* Flag cached or reused proofs, a `kid` or private members, query in `htu`, the plain endpoint used despite an mTLS alias, `DateTime.UtcNow`, a short or non-random `jti`, synchronous signing, or `ath` on the wrong proofs. <sub>Identity ADR-1176; Identity ADR-1286; Identity ADR-1300</sub>
- **Never resend a request through a generic retry when it carries a DPoP proof, a client assertion, an authorization code or refresh token, or any body. Only a `use_dpop_nonce` challenge sends it once more: buffer the content before the first send, rebuild the form from a fresh copy of the caller's parameters, run client authentication again, and sign a new proof with the supplied nonce.** DPoP `jti` and client assertions are single-use (RFC 9449 §11.1), OAuth endpoints honor no idempotency key, and unbuffered content can't be sent twice. *Check:* Flag retry predicates that don't exclude DPoP or bodied requests, nonce retries that loop more than once, reuse an already-sent form or proof, reuse a client assertion, or skip buffering; also check the `DPoP-Nonce` header is recorded from every response. <sub>Identity ADR-1286; Identity ADR-1291; Identity ADR-1336</sub>
- **Present an access token the way it was issued: a DPoP-bound token as `Authorization: DPoP` with a proof of its key (retrying a nonce challenge exactly once), other tokens as Bearer, and use the endpoint's mTLS alias when the client authenticates with mutual TLS. Don't attach a DPoP proof to revocation requests.** Bound tokens are accepted only with proof of possession (RFC 9449 §7, §9; RFC 8705 §5), and neither RFC 7009 nor RFC 9449 defines a revocation proof. *Check:* Flag protected-endpoint calls that always send Bearer, ignore the binding, skip `mtls_endpoint_aliases`, or add a DPoP header to revocation calls. <sub>Identity ADR-1301; Identity ADR-1286</sub>
- **When a client uses mutual TLS and the provider publishes an `mtls_endpoint_aliases` entry, send the request to the alias and use that URL for the DPoP `htu`, the DPoP nonce cache key and the authentication context; validate every alias with the same https-or-loopback rule as other discovered endpoints; and always send `client_id` with `tls_client_auth` and `self_signed_tls_client_auth`.** RFC 8705 §2 and §5 require it, and an alias receives credentials so needs the same transport guarantee. *Check:* Flag mTLS requests to the plain endpoint despite an alias, DPoP values keyed on the original endpoint, unvalidated aliases, or mTLS authenticators without `client_id`. <sub>Identity ADR-1300</sub>
- **Emit the access token's `cnf` and `token_type` from the evaluated binding: `cnf.jkt` (RFC 7638 thumbprint) with `token_type: DPoP`, or `cnf.x5t#S256` (SHA-256 of the certificate) with Bearer for mTLS. Bind to a certificate only when the client's binding requirement is true, answer `invalid_request` when it requires binding but presents no certificate, and refuse a missing required sender constraint before redeeming the code or rotating the refresh token.** RFC 9449 and RFC 8705 §3 define these members; advertised support never forces binding; a refusal after redemption has already spent the grant. *Check:* Flag a DPoP token answered as Bearer or the reverse, wrong thumbprints, binding keyed off server support or mere certificate presence, a silent Bearer when binding is required, or the client-level check placed after redemption or rotation. <sub>Identity ADR-1097; Identity ADR-1158</sub>
- **Make the token revocation endpoint answer 200 to every authenticated request whether the token was revoked, unknown, expired or non-revocable, and 400 `invalid_request` only when `token` is missing. Treat revoking a self-contained JWT access token as an accepted no-op, with no per-token denylist or per-request revocation lookup.** RFC 7009 requires this so the endpoint isn't an oracle, and a denylist would add the per-call state a stateless JWT exists to avoid. *Check:* Flag non-200 results or responses that differ by token state, and new access-token denylists or revocation lookups in access-token validation. <sub>Identity ADR-1028</sub>
- **Make the introspection endpoint answer `400 invalid_request` only when `token` is missing and 200 otherwise; for an inactive token (invalid, expired, revoked, foreign, wrong caller, or a refresh token whose family passed its horizon) return exactly `{"active": false}`.** RFC 7662 forbids revealing why a token failed, and introspection must not call active a token the refresh grant would refuse. *Check:* Flag extra members or error details next to `active: false`, non-200 statuses for bad tokens, or refresh-token introspection that ignores the family horizon. <sub>Identity ADR-1168; Identity ADR-1297</sub>
- **Give a JWT introspection response (RFC 9701) `typ` `token-introspection+jwt`, only `iss`, `aud` (the resource server) and `iat` at top level, the result under `token_introspection`, and never a top-level `sub` or `exp`.** Without top-level `sub` or `exp` it can't be mistaken for an access token. *Check:* Flag another `typ`, flattened result claims, or a top-level `sub`/`exp`. <sub>Identity ADR-1168</sub>
- **In token exchange, choose the validation policy by token type: `access_token` under the access-token policy, `id_token` under the ID-token policy, `jwt` only when it validates as one of those, and any other type `invalid_request`. Reject a client's own (no resource owner) token as `subject_token` with `invalid_grant` while accepting it as `actor_token`.** A generic `jwt` must not let an introspection response or logout token be exchanged (RFC 8693, RFC 9701 §8.1), and a token with no resource owner names no user. *Check:* Flag `jwt` accepted with generic validation, unknown types accepted, wrong error codes, or a client token refused as actor. <sub>Identity ADR-1101; Identity ADR-1167; Identity ADR-1466</sub>
- **For delegation token exchange, require the actor token to belong to the requester, the subject token's `may_act.sub` to equal the actor's `sub` (and `client_id`/`iss` when present), and subject and actor to differ; issue an `act` claim that nests any existing `act`. Validate only the exchanged subject (with the tenant its token was validated under); don't ask for the actor to be validated as a subject.** This is RFC 8693's act/may_act handling; the actor's token is already checked by issued-token validation. *Check:* Flag a skipped may_act comparison, subject == actor allowed, missing or overwritten `act`; before reporting missing actor subject validation, confirm the actor token goes through issued-token validation. <sub>Identity ADR-1101; Identity ADR-1225</sub>
- **In a token-exchange response, default `requested_token_type` to `access_token`, return a requested ID token in the `access_token` field with `token_type` `N_A`, and always include `issued_token_type`.** RFC 8693 §2.2.1 requires this format. *Check:* Flag a missing `issued_token_type`, an ID token in another field or with another token_type, or a different default. <sub>Identity ADR-1101</sub>
- **Bind a stored bearer credential issued to one client (device code, `auth_req_id`) to that client: right after the grant lookup and before expiry, status or polling checks, answer another client with `invalid_grant` without consuming it. In a polling grant, then validate the subject, consume the approved request once, and issue tokens.** RFC 8628 §3.4 and CIBA Core §11 bind these credentials; checking first avoids leaking grant state and prevents theft and replay. *Check:* Check the order: client binding (no consume), subject validation, one-time consume, issuance. <sub>Identity ADR-1225; Identity ADR-1085</sub>
- **Answer a device or CIBA token poll with `slow_down` when it arrives within the polling interval of the last recorded poll, `authorization_pending` while pending, `access_denied` when denied and `expired_token` past expiry, all as 400; record the last-poll time only in the pending branch, and keep that state on the pending request record rather than in a separate rate limiter, cache or table.** RFC 8628 defines these responses; recording after a decision would throttle completion; the record already carries tenant scope and expiry. *Check:* Check the interval comparison, where the timestamp is updated, the codes and status, and look for new limiter or cache infrastructure for polling. <sub>Identity ADR-1059; Identity ADR-1085</sub>
- **Let an approve or deny decision on a pending device or CIBA request change only a still-pending request, through a read-modify-write of the grant payload, and revoke a user-code pointer exactly once.** Concurrent or repeated decisions must not overwrite a decided request, and a user code is single-use. *Check:* Check that pending status is tested inside the read-modify-write and the pointer uses revoke-once semantics. <sub>Identity ADR-1059</sub>
- **Reject a CIBA backchannel authentication request unless exactly one of `login_hint`, `login_hint_token` or `id_token_hint` is present and, for ping or push, a `client_notification_token`. - **Send back-channel logout only as the tenant's discovery advertises: nothing while `backchannel_logout_supported` is false, no `sid` while `backchannel_logout_session_supported` is false; issue a signed `logout_token` with `typ` `logout+jwt` and `iss`, `aud`, `iat`, `jti`, `events` and `sid`/`sub`. Treat front-channel logout as a best-effort addition that never disables back-channel delivery, appending `iss`/`sid` only while `frontchannel_logout_session_supported` is on.** The OP must behave as it advertises, Back-Channel Logout defines the token, and back-channel stays the reliable mechanism. *Check:* Flag notifiers ignoring discovery settings, missing `typ` or claims, front-channel paths that skip back-channel, or unconditional `iss`/`sid` on front-channel URIs. <sub>Identity ADR-1380; Identity ADR-1088</sub>
- **Emit the session's opaque `sid` in the ID token, every subject-bound access token (RFC 9068 §2.2.1) and the logout token when sessions are supported, and omit it for a token issued without a session; compute `session_state` as a salted SHA-256 over client id, the redirect URI's origin and the OP browser state, only while session management is enabled.** Relying parties and logout identify sessions by `sid`, and Session Management 1.0's check_session_iframe recomputes this exact value. *Check:* Flag missing `sid`, placeholder `sid` without a session, or a session_state without salt, with another hash or origin, or stamped while disabled. <sub>Identity ADR-1220; Identity ADR-1088</sub>
- **Issue a refresh token only when the client requested `offline_access` and the `refresh_token` grant is supported; by default don't rotate refresh tokens of confidential clients or tokens bound to a DPoP key or certificate unless the client opts in.** Issuance is tied to both conditions, and FAPI 2.0 §5.3.2.1 forbids rotation for sender-constrained confidential clients, where a lost rotation loses the session. *Check:* Flag refresh tokens issued without both checks, defaults that rotate bound or confidential tokens, or FAPI profiles inheriting 'always rotate'. <sub>Identity ADR-1026; Identity ADR-1216</sub>

- **Under a sliding refresh policy, expire each token at the sliding lifetime from issue or last use capped at the family's fixed horizon; under absolute, at the horizon. Include in every token response carrying a refresh token (any grant, retry, CIBA push) `refresh_token_expires_in` as whole seconds to the family horizon.** Sliding promises extension only up to an absolute maximum, and clients bound sessions by a horizon that never moves later. *Check:* Flag uncapped sliding expiry, absolute expiry from issuance, or a missing or per-token `refresh_token_expires_in`. <sub>Identity ADR-1297</sub>
- **In a client, present a rotating refresh token at most once cluster-wide: guard each refresh with a single-flight lease keyed by a fingerprint of the refresh token (not the session version), re-read the session under the lease, have losers wait with backoff and never present a token whose lease another holds (fail, such as 503, on timeout), run the token request and write-back with `CancellationToken.None`, and merge and retry a write-back that loses a concurrency race.** Presenting a rotated token twice revokes the family (RFC 9700 §4.14.2), unrelated writes bump the version, and a dropped write or aborted caller loses the only copy of the new token. *Check:* Flag refreshes without a lease, leases keyed by version or session id, timeout fallbacks using the old token, caller cancellation passed to refresh or persistence, or conflicts that discard the update. <sub>Identity ADR-1291</sub>
- **In a client, treat a token response without `expires_in` as already expiring, read `refresh_token_expires_in` leniently (ignore a non-positive or non-whole value), and use it only to lower the session's and cookie's lifetime, never to extend it.** A missing lifetime can't be trusted and the advisory, non-standard member must neither fail a response nor lengthen a session. *Check:* Flag assumed default lifetimes, strict parsing that rejects the response, or session expiry set without taking the minimum. <sub>Identity ADR-1291; Identity ADR-1297; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **An OIDC client requests `openid` plus the configured scopes, each once, and never adds `offline_access` on its own.** `offline_access` asks for a grant outliving the login session, and some OPs then detach it so back-channel logout never reaches the client. *Check:* Flag automatic or `scopes_supported`-conditional `offline_access` or duplicate scopes. <sub>Identity ADR-1291</sub>
- **Accept a UserInfo response only in the format the client registered—`application/jwt` when it registered `userinfo_signed_response_alg`, JSON otherwise—with a matching `Accept` header; treat `exp`, `nbf`, `iat` in a UserInfo JWT as optional; and reject an unsigned response whose `iss` is present but not a string equal to the provider's issuer.** A JSON answer to a signing client strips the signature, OIDC Core §5.3.2 requires no lifetime claims, and a foreign `iss` relabels claims. *Check:* Flag branching on response Content-Type, JSON fallback, unrequested JWT validation, required lifetime claims on UserInfo, or `sub` checked but not `iss`. <sub>Identity ADR-1301; Identity review of #420</sub>
- **Treat OIDC `claims` request `value`/`values` as advisory and emit only the subject's actual claims; don't fail issuance or UserInfo for a missing essential claim except an essential `id_token.acr` with `values` the principal's `acr` doesn't satisfy (`access_denied`); refuse a disabled optional parameter (such as `claims` when unsupported) with a not-supported error instead of ignoring it.** The OP must not fabricate claims, `essential` is best effort except for acr, and an ignored parameter hides that a request wasn't honored. *Check:* Flag claims copied from the request, errors on missing non-acr essentials, unsatisfied acr not rejected, or disabled parameters silently skipped. <sub>Identity ADR-1039</sub>
- **Resolve `acr` at authentication time through a replaceable asynchronous resolver and store it with the authentication event (omitting it when nothing yields a value); have the authenticating component stamp RFC 8176 `amr` values; always include `auth_time` in the ID token when `max_age` or essential `auth_time` applies (synthesizing only then and only for the ID token) and in the access token only when the principal has it.** These are properties of the authentication event; OIDC Core makes auth_time conditionally mandatory and RFC 9068 includes it only when available. *Check:* Flag literal or lazily derived acr, placeholder acr, authenticators without amr, or unconditional, synthesized-for-access-token or missing auth_time. <sub>Identity ADR-1039</sub>
- **A claim-projection handler skips empty values and doesn't add a claim type another handler already supplied.** Empty and duplicated claims add noise and conflicts to tokens. *Check:* Check handlers test emptiness and the existing claim collection before adding. <sub>Identity ADR-1055</sub>
- **Record consent as both the scopes the subject decided and the subset granted, prompting only for scopes outside the decided set; make `prompt=consent` force a fresh decision only on the initial request, not the resumed continuation; answer `prompt=none` needing consent with `consent_required` and audit it.** Granted-only records re-prompt for denied scopes forever, a resumed continuation still carries prompt=consent and would loop, and prompt=none forbids UI. *Check:* Flag granted-only consent models, prompt=consent checks ignoring continuation, or prompt=none paths that show UI, use another error or skip audit. <sub>Identity ADR-1081</sub>
- **When a sign-in refusal or consent denial belongs to a pending authorization request, answer it at the client's redirect URI with `access_denied` and `state`, never a local error page or a redirect home. Decide whether a refused subject is challenged from the end user's standing, not the error code: a refused standing returns an error for every `prompt`, other refusals challenge or return `login_required` for `prompt=none`.** The client must get an answer (RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1, OIDC Core §3.1.2.6), and challenging a blocked user causes a login loop. *Check:* Flag deny or refusal paths that redirect home or render errors, other codes, re-challenging every refused subject, or branching on the error code. <sub>Identity ADR-1229; Identity ADR-1081; Identity ADR-1062</sub>
- **When a subject is validated outside a protocol request, pass a null request rather than a fabricated one; the validator skips only request-dependent checks (`max_age`, `idp:` acr_values, essential acr).** A fabricated request misrepresents the context. *Check:* Flag placeholder requests built for subject validation, or validators skipping more than request-dependent checks on null. <sub>Identity ADR-1225</sub>
- **Answer a password-grant request with a rejected credential with `invalid_grant`, using `unsupported_grant_type` only when no handler for the grant is registered.** A rejected credential is an authentication failure, not a missing capability. *Check:* Flag the codes swapped in password-grant handlers. <sub>Identity ADR-1051</sub>
- **Deliver authorization responses through response-mode handlers resolved by name, never a switch or list over `query`/`fragment`/`form_post`; decide JWT securing from the handler's declared property, not a `.jwt` suffix; check `response_modes_supported` once against both the written and resolved mode; and when no handler serves the mode or the tenant refuses it, answer 400 without redirecting (`invalid_request` for a request object naming it).** Response modes are an open vocabulary, narrowing must cover shorthand and resolution, and an unserved mode can't carry an error back. *Check:* Flag mode switches, enumerated validation, `EndsWith(".jwt")`, checks on only one form or repeated, or redirected or defaulted unsupported-mode errors. <sub>Identity ADR-1201; Identity ADR-1202</sub>
- **Issue a JARM response JWT with `iss` the issuer, `aud` the `client_id`, `exp` a short configured lifetime after `iat`, every response parameter as a claim except the RFC 9207 `iss`, and secure error responses the same way.** The client verifies origin and integrity, and errors need the same protection. *Check:* Flag missing `aud`/`exp`, duplicated `iss`, or error paths bypassing JWT securing. <sub>Identity ADR-1201</sub>
- **Don't treat protocol vocabularies (grant types, client-authentication methods, response types and modes, key types, session-termination reasons, profiles) as closed sets: accept registered values from consumers or sibling packages and compare open string vocabularies ordinally, passing unknown values through unchanged.** Well-known constants name members of open vocabularies; they don't close them. *Check:* Flag enums, switches or validation rejecting unknown values where the vocabulary is open, or case- or culture-sensitive comparison. <sub>Identity ADR-1276; Identity ADR-1112</sub>
- **Never derive a registry or wire name from another identifier by string rewriting (such as lowercasing `HashAlgorithmName.Name`); map each known name explicitly and fail for unknown ones. Validate a caller-supplied RFC 6920 Named Information hash name against `1*unreserved`, requiring the exact registry name for a known hash.** No trait should be guessed from a name, and a known hash must never be mislabeled. *Check:* Flag `ToLowerInvariant`/`Replace` transforms into registry names, or `ni:` code accepting names without unreserved or known-mapping checks. <sub>Identity ADR-1119</sub>
- **Reference OAuth, OpenID Connect and JOSE wire names (parameters, error codes, grant and response types, discovery members, media types, well-known paths, PKCE methods, algorithm codes) through the single shared protocol-vocabulary constants, taking claim names from the shared JOSE claim-name constants; don't write them as literals, redeclare them in local constant classes, or alias a different concept that only shares the spelling.** Each wire name should exist once so copies can't drift, and aliasing unrelated concepts couples them. *Check:* Flag literals like "client_id", "invalid_grant", "S256", "ES256", "sub" or new constant classes where shared constants exist, and same-spelled settings aliased to discovery constants. *Note:* This applies to test code too; literals inside static JSON fixtures such as a realm export are fine. <sub>Identity ADR-1276; Identity review of #350; Identity outcomes of #590</sub>
- **Make an OpenID Provider's authorization, end-session and post-sign-in continue endpoints accept `GET` (and `POST` where the spec requires), and don't report their state changes on `GET` as safe-GET or antiforgery violations.** RFC 6749 §3.1, OIDC Core §3.1.2.1 and RP-Initiated Logout §2 require GET, and browsers arrive by redirect. *Check:* Flag mappings dropping GET or POST on these endpoints; don't raise safe-GET findings there. <sub>Identity ADR-1314; Identity AGENTS.md</sub>
- **In production code, keep a protocol endpoint thin—guard method and content type, authenticate the client, load a strongly typed request message, dispatch replaceable steps, render—and never read parameters by string key with `form.TryGetValue(...)`.** Typed messages give consistent parsing, serialization, extensibility and OpenAPI metadata, and keep steps replaceable. *Check:* Flag handlers that parse form or query by hand or inline validation and business logic. <sub>Identity ADR-1086; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **In production code, model a server-advertised capability and a client-registered requirement as two settings, with a rule rejecting the requirement where support is off, naming the requirement `require_` plus its RFC metadata member.** Advertising support must never force every client to use it. *Check:* Flag one setting that both advertises and forces a capability, or misnamed requirements. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Every OpenID protocol endpoint returns `x-fapi-interaction-id`, echoing the request's value verbatim only when it is a canonical hyphenated UUID and otherwise generating one, set by one filter on the protocol endpoint group before `next` runs and outside the rate-limit and environment filters.** FAPI 1.0 §6.2.1-11 requires it on every response, including refusals, and echoing arbitrary strings carries untrusted input into logs. *Check:* Flag unvalidated echoes, case changes, per-endpoint or post-`next` setting, endpoints outside the group, or filter ordering that skips refused requests. <sub>Identity ADR-1498</sub>
- **In server-driven content negotiation for OAuth/OIDC responses, select an alternate formatter only for an explicit `type/subtype` in `Accept`; `*/*`, `type/*` or no `Accept` yields JSON.** Programmatic callers send `*/*` and expect the JSON wire default; only browsers listing `text/html` should get HTML. *Check:* Flag wildcard matches that select HTML or other non-JSON formatters. <sub>Identity ADR-1114</sub>
- **Parse a protocol response as JSON only when the body is non-empty and the media type is JSON (`application/json`, `application/jwk-set+json`); write responses with strict UTF-8, adding `charset=utf-8` to text types (for example passing a strict UTF-8 `contentEncoding` to `TypedResults.Text`/`Content`) but no charset to types that define none such as `application/jwt`.** Success bodies may be empty (RFC 7009 §2.2), wrongly typed bodies shouldn't be parsed, and content must be strictly encoded. *Check:* Flag deserialization without media-type checks, failures on empty success bodies, `Text`/`Content` calls without the encoding argument, or charset on `application/jwt`. <sub>Identity ADR-1285; Identity ADR-1266</sub>
- **Every HTTP API error is an RFC 9457 problem document; a problem that asks the caller to wait sets both `Retry-After` and a `retryAfterSeconds` extension member (whole seconds, rounded up, at least 1) through one shared helper and never puts the wait in the detail text.** Bare statuses break the contract, and browser fetch layers drop headers while prose isn't machine-readable. *Check:* Flag bare `NotFound()`/`StatusCode(4xx)`, only one of header or member, truncated or zero seconds, or durations in `detail`. <sub>Identity ADR-1483</sub>
- **Send concurrency tokens in `ETag` as quoted strong entity tags through the shared formatter; evaluate `If-Match` with strong comparison (never stripping `W/`) and answer 412 on mismatch or a save-time concurrency conflict; evaluate `If-None-Match` with weak comparison per RFC 9110 §13.1.2 (`*` or a weak match gives 304, a missing or malformed header is no match, no bare tokens).** RFC 9110 §8.8.3 and §13.1 define these forms, and checking stops stale writes from silently overwriting changes. *Check:* Flag unquoted or weak ETags, hand-built tags, weak or `W/`-trimmed If-Match comparison, ignored If-Match, non-412 conflicts, strong-only If-None-Match, missing `*`, or errors on a malformed If-None-Match. *Note:* Don't report a management API accepting a lone bare token (no quotes, commas, white space or `W/`, compared ordinally) in `If-Match` only; and don't report `If-None-Match` refusing bare tokens. <sub>Identity ADR-1513; Identity ADR-1320; Identity outcomes of #832</sub>
- **Don't put an ETag or continuation token on a caller-specific, unpaged list response.** The answer depends on the caller, so a shared validator or paging token misleads. *Check:* Flag such headers on responses with per-caller fields. <sub>Identity ADR-1465</sub>
- **Compare integer HTTP status codes against `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.StatusCodes` constants, not `(int)HttpStatusCode.X` casts or numeric literals.** One constants source keeps comparisons consistent. *Check:* Flag casts or literals like `200`/`404` used as status values, including in tests. <sub>Identity review of #320</sub>
- **Retry an outbound HTTP request only when it's safe to send twice—a bodiless GET or HEAD—and only for transient failures (408, 429, 5xx, per-attempt timeout, `HttpRequestException`), with exponential jittered backoff bounded by a total timeout that `Retry-After` can't extend; give every outbound call its own timeout and read bodies under a size limit.** Repeating bodied or non-idempotent requests duplicates side effects, jitter avoids synchronized retries, and calls must not hang or exhaust memory. *Check:* Flag retries covering POST/PUT/PATCH or content, other 4xx retries, constant delays, missing attempt-timeout handling, waits on Retry-After, missing timeouts or resilience, or unbounded `ReadAsStringAsync`. *Note:* For fetches of caller-supplied URLs (such as `jwks_uri`), also don't retry connection or name-resolution errors and ignore `Retry-After`, since the guard's refusal is deterministic. <sub>Identity ADR-1336; Identity ADR-1315; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **Make a remote key-creation call (KMS) exactly once with SDK retries off, keep an explicit SDK retry policy for repeatable calls (read, sign, decrypt, destroy), and add no retry layer of your own.** A retried creation can create an orphaned key never destroyed. *Check:* Check creation clients set retries to zero and look for custom retry loops around KMS calls. <sub>Identity ADR-1474</sub>
- **Make a BFF a confidential OAuth client authenticating with `private_key_jwt` or mTLS, using authorization code with PKCE S256, PAR when advertised and DPoP when supported, relying only on standard OP metadata with no provider-specific adapter; and don't add OP settings or descriptors a BFF needs, or implement implicit, hybrid, password or token-mediating flows for a browser client.** This is current best practice; the BFF must work with any compliant provider, and those flows expose tokens to script. *Check:* Flag client secrets instead of assertions, ignored PAR/DPoP metadata, hard-coded paths or provider branches, BFF-only provider settings, `token`/`id_token` response types, password grants, or tokens returned to the SPA. <sub>Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity ADR-1294</sub>
- **A BFF answers a guarded API or user-info call without a live session with 401 and the `session_required` problem type, never a redirect; its user-info endpoint only reads the session and never slides idle expiry; and it adds no SSE, WebSocket or pub/sub push for session-end events.** The 401 is the one signal frontends rely on across replicas, polling must not keep sessions alive, and push streams starve the per-origin connection limit. *Check:* Flag redirects, 403s or plain 401s on guarded endpoints, idle sliding on user-info, or new `text/event-stream`, WebSocket or pub/sub for logout notifications. <sub>Identity ADR-1434</sub>
- **A BFF-served frontend that learns its session ended (logout, 401 `session_required`, expiry, failed refresh) broadcasts it to other tabs via `BroadcastChannel` and shows a sign-in screen whose button starts the login, never navigating to login on its own; it probes with the anti-forgery header, rechecks on `visibilitychange`, and signs out by POSTing the logout form with `sid` and a return URL.** Self-navigating tabs race and loop, BroadcastChannel alone misses back-channel logouts, hidden tabs' timers are throttled, and logout is a sid-bound form post. *Check:* Flag `window.location` set to login from session-ended handlers, 401 handlers not notifying tabs, missing anti-forgery headers or visibility rechecks, or GET sign-out links. <sub>Identity ADR-1434; Identity ADR-1438</sub>
- **Don't classify a cross-site or redirected top-level navigation by `Sec-Fetch-Site`; key it on the method, `Sec-Fetch-Mode` absent or `navigate`, and the Strict session cookie being absent, and bound any automatic reload or retry with a short-lived marker such as a `__Host-` Secure HttpOnly cookie with Max-Age about 60.** Browsers label the same navigation differently, and an unbounded reload loops forever. *Check:* Flag branches on `Sec-Fetch-Site` or reload responses without a marker. <sub>Identity ADR-1292</sub>
- **A hub (WebSocket/SignalR) request never writes cookies to the upgraded response; it slides the session and gets tokens through the connection's in-memory session handle.** The upgraded response has already started, and there's no `HttpContext` after the connection opens. *Check:* Flag session refresh or `Set-Cookie` writes on hub paths. <sub>Identity ADR-1435</sub>
- **Give each OAuth client in one deployment a unique callback URI, validated across all configured clients, and make the client selectable from the URLs the OP is told (callback, back-channel logout, JWKS), not only by routing.** The OP and browser reach these receivers, so they must resolve the right client. *Check:* Flag configuration validation missing duplicate-callback checks, or client selection that only works via routing such as `RequireHost`. <sub>Identity ADR-1442</sub>
- **Serve interactive sign-in, consent and logout pages from the OP's own origin as native HTML form POSTs carrying the antiforgery token, give their controls explicit stable ids (`username`, `password`, `login`, `consent-allow`, `consent-deny`) in both server-rendered pages and the frontend bundle, and have a page hosting a mountable bundle write `<base href="{mount path}/">` first in `<head>` with page-relative form actions.** Cookies, antiforgery and `ReturnUrl` only round-trip on one origin, conformance suites find fields by stable id, and the bundle resolves paths against `document.baseURI`. *Check:* Flag fetch/XHR or cross-origin form submission, skipped antiforgery, generated or renamed ids, or a missing `<base href>` or root-level actions. <sub>Identity ADR-1062; Identity ADR-1193</sub>
- **Build tenant-relative redirect, challenge and cookie paths from `Request.PathBase` and the request's route values, and in production code generate published URLs from the named route with the tenant's authority, passing a copy of `RouteValues` to any template binder.** The tenant scope may have ended when the cookie is written, endpoints sit under a configurable prefix, and the binder consumes the values it's given. *Check:* Flag ambient tenant accessors in redirect code, string-built absolute URLs, or live `RouteValues` passed to `TemplateBinder`/`LinkGenerator`. <sub>Identity ADR-1193; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Read forwarded client-certificate headers as a comma-separated chain with the leaf first, passing the rest as intermediates; match X.500 distinguished names with RFC 4517 `distinguishedNameMatch`, never by DER bytes or `X500DistinguishedName.Name` strings.** The proxy forwards the whole chain, and CAs differ in string type and case that the RFC treats as equal. *Check:* Flag whole-value decoding, wrong leaf selection, dropped intermediates, or `RawData`/`Name` equality for DNs. <sub>Identity docs/hosting-analysis.md; Identity ADR-1173</sub>
- **Build OCSP requests to the RFC 5019 lightweight profile (one SHA-1 `CertID`, no requestor name, signature or nonce; GET when the URL is at most 255 characters, otherwise POST as `application/ocsp-request`), fall through to CRLs when OCSP fails or answers `unknown`, and in indirect CRLs carry `certificateIssuer` forward, match serial plus issuer and don't count `removeFromCRL` as revoked.** Pre-produced responders can't echo nonces, PKIs with both sources must keep working when OCSP is down, and indirect CRLs list several CAs. *Check:* Flag nonces, signatures or multiple CertIDs, fixed methods, terminal results on OCSP failure, serial-only matching, per-entry issuer reset, or removeFromCRL treated as revoked. <sub>Identity ADR-1259</sub>
- **Resolve SD-JWT disclosures per RFC 9901 §7.1, refusing each ambiguity with a distinct failure code (repeated digests, shared disclosures, object/array mismatches, collisions, unreferenced disclosures, misplaced reserved names, malformed `_sd`/`...`); compute digests over the encoding as received and `sd_hash` over the presentation up to the last `~`; validate a KB-JWT as `kb+jwt` with holder key, allowed algorithms, audience and an `iat` within skew and maximum age; and refuse to make a profile's required claims disclosable at issuance.** Ambiguity lets holders change what verifiers read, re-encoding breaks digests, freshness stops replay, and verifiers check required claims before resolving disclosures. *Check:* Check each refusal case and code, digest inputs, KB-JWT `typ`, audience and both freshness bounds, and issuer path validation of required claims. <sub>Identity ADR-1405; Identity outcomes of #552</sub>
- **CBOR/COSE writers produce RFC 8949 §4.2.1 core deterministic encoding (definite lengths, shortest integers, map keys sorted bytewise by encoded label, not `CborConformanceMode.Canonical`) and write an empty protected header as a zero-length byte string; readers accept either empty form, authenticate protected bytes as received without enforcing map order, refuse untagged messages unless the caller names the type, and map a binary `kid` to text through the one shared mapping (UTF-8 when valid and not starting with `h'`, else `h'...'` diagnostic notation).** Canonical mode sorts by length first, RFC 9052 requires determinism only for what the library builds, and every component must map kids the same way. *Check:* Flag Canonical mode, indefinite lengths, insertion-order maps, encoded empty maps for protected headers, reader canonicalization findings, guessed untagged types, or ad-hoc kid conversions. <sub>Identity ADR-1409</sub>
- **A cross-replica change announcement carries only an identifier of what changed, never the data; receivers re-read or evict.** It's a cache-drop hint; storage stays the source of truth and state may not serialize. *Check:* Flag broadcast messages serializing entity state, settings or secrets. <sub>Identity ADR-1205</sub>
- **Count a daily quota in one fixed window per UTC calendar day expiring at the next UTC midnight, judged after the per-minute rate limits.** UTC gives every replica and tenant one boundary a tenant can't reset by changing zones, and refused requests shouldn't spend the quota. *Check:* Flag local, tenant-zone or sliding 24-hour windows, or a quota stage before per-minute limits. <sub>Identity ADR-1198</sub>
- **A who-am-I or capabilities route without an authority check answers an anonymous caller 401 and declares 401 but not 403, never an empty 200.** An empty 200 hides a missing or expired token (RFC 6750 §3), and without an authority check 403 can't happen. *Check:* Flag empty 200s for anonymous callers or declared 403s without authorization. <sub>Identity ADR-1044</sub>
- **Never treat an unsupported `ui_locales` value as an error; select locales by RFC 4647 §3.4 lookup in preference order, case-insensitively, applying the tenant's supported-locales ceiling to the fallback too; carry the preference across interactive pages in the redirect's `ui_locales` query and a hidden form field, not by reloading the parked request or a cookie. Don't ask account-management pages outside an authorization or end-session flow to carry it.** OIDC Core §3.1.2.1 says unsupported locales SHOULD NOT error, the ceiling keeps rendering consistent with discovery, and per-request store reads or cookies add cost and state. *Check:* Flag validators rejecting `ui_locales`, exact or case-sensitive matching, uncapped fallbacks, store or cookie lookups for locale, or dropped values between flow pages. <sub>Identity ADR-1402; Identity outcomes of #548</sub>
- **Reject removing a resource's last owner with 409 Conflict.** A resource keeps at least one owner. *Check:* Check owner-revocation endpoints for a last-owner guard. <sub>Identity ADR-1417</sub>
- **Document a structured record emitted for others (audit record, webhook, event) in `docs/` in the same change, give it a schema version whose minor version is bumped when a field is added, omit absent members and empty arrays instead of writing null or `[]`, use the same field names in logs, spans and metrics, and for audit events use UUIDv7 ids and UTC RFC 3339 times with a `Z` suffix.** It is a consumer contract, and UUIDv7 sorts by time. *Check:* Flag payload changes without docs or version updates, `WriteNull` or empty arrays, mismatched telemetry names, `Guid.NewGuid()` event ids, or offset times. *Note:* The version bump applies where the repository tracks changes; a repository whose conventions say it is pre-release and tracks no changes may change the format outright. <sub>Identity docs/audit-records.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **In production code, give a JSON-deserialized DTO a `[JsonExtensionData] Dictionary<string, JsonElement>? ExtensionData` member.** Unrecognized wire members round-trip instead of being dropped. *Check:* Flag deserialized DTOs lacking it. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Forward HTTP requests through YARP's `IHttpForwarder` rather than a hand-written `HttpClient` proxy.** It handles streaming, hop-by-hop headers and protocol edge cases. *Check:* Flag proxies copying requests and responses by hand. <sub>Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **When code or a script reads a paged API (GraphQL `first:` connections, REST `per_page`) and relies on the full result, page through it (for example `gh api --paginate --slurp`) or check `pageInfo.hasNextPage` and report partial results; read the newest item with `last:`; and when replacing a CLI list call with REST search, pass the sort and order the caller relies on (`sort=updated&order=desc`). Don't report a single-page call whose adjacent comment states the cap and why the filtered result stays below it.** Items past the first page vanish silently, and search defaults to best-match order. *Check:* Flag `first: N` without `pageInfo`, `per_page` without paging or a justifying comment, last items taken from a `first:` window, or search calls missing sort parameters. <sub>project-template outcomes of #124; project-template outcomes of #146; project-template outcomes of #148; project-template outcomes of #244</sub>
- **Don't report a partial-update API call as missing a body field until you've checked the API reference: if the field is optional and the call runs only when the resource is already in the required state, omitting it is correct.** Such findings were declined where the reference marks every body field optional. *Check:* Read the documented required flags and the guard before the call. <sub>project-template outcomes of #140</sub>
- **Probe an HTTPS-only ASP.NET Core pod with `scheme: HTTPS` and a `Host` header that `AllowedHosts` accepts; startup and liveness probes call the liveness endpoint and only readiness calls the readiness endpoint.** The kubelet sends the pod IP as Host, and liveness must not check dependencies. *Check:* Inspect probe scheme, `httpHeaders` Host and each probe's path. <sub>Identity ADR-1458</sub>
